title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the polynomial removal conjecture for ordered binary matrices: a fixed 66 x 66 pattern H and, for every h, a binary matrix of order n = (386h+2)2^h that is (386h+2)^-2-far from H-free but has at most a 2^-h fraction of that many ordered copies per n^132. The first lesson builds the pattern and the tree-indexed host matrices; the second shows that every copy of H passes through one of 2^h diagonal leaf cells, by an anchor-rigidity argument and the order relations of the tree; the third proves the distance bound by sampling one root-to-leaf path and propagating forced values, and derives the theorem and a lower bound for canonical row-column sampling.
